title: Day 956: IDF Documents 19 Hamas Ceasefire Violations May 6–20 — Hamas Producing Hundreds of IEDs and Anti-Tank Rockets Monthly, Running Military Training During Truce
detail: On May 20, 2026 (Day 956 / Ceasefire Day 223), the IDF released its bi-weekly ceasefire compliance report covering May 6–20, 2026, documenting 19 Palestinian violations of the October 10, 2025 Gaza ceasefire. The IDF report — published simultaneously with the Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD) / Long War Journal analysis — detailed Hamas's systematic military reconstitution activities during the ceasefire period, including: production of hundreds of IEDs and anti-tank rockets monthly inside Gaza; weapons smuggling operations through tunnels and commercial channels; and Hamas military training exercises conducted openly in areas under its control. The report came three days after Hamas appointed Mohammed Odeh — former Hamas military intelligence chief and October 7 attack intelligence planner — as the new Al-Qassam Brigades commander, following the IDF's killing of predecessor Izz al-Din al-Haddad on May 15–16. The documentation of Hamas military reconstitution during the ceasefire reinforced Israeli government arguments that Hamas was using the ceasefire period to rebuild offensive military capabilities rather than transition toward Phase Two implementation. By contrast, the Palestinian side documented over 2,400 Israeli ceasefire violations in the same seven-month period, including airstrikes, civilian shootings, and territorial expansion beyond the ceasefire Yellow Line. The IDF report's 19-violation count covers only violations the IDF chose to formally document, covering the specific May 6–20 window. The IDF figures and Palestinian documentation reflect fundamentally different methodologies and political framing of what constitutes a 'violation.' As of May 20, 2026, Israel controlled approximately 60% of Gaza's territory — far beyond the ceasefire demarcation boundaries — while Phase Two negotiations remained in total collapse. The IDF violations report provides specific evidentiary support for Israel's argument that Hamas's continued military reconstitution makes Phase Two's disarmament requirements impossible without renewed military pressure.

media.caption: Hamas replaces military wing leader; IDF reports 19 Gaza ceasefire violations May 6–20 — FDD / Long War Journal, May 20, 2026

title: Day 956: Board of Peace Six-Month Progress Report Published — Hamas Named 'Principal Obstacle' to Phase Two; Ceasefire Systematically Stalled Since October 10, 2025
detail: On May 20, 2026 (Day 956 / Ceasefire Day 223), the Board of Peace — the Gaza ceasefire oversight body established under Trump's 20-point peace plan and chaired by former UN envoy Nickolay Mladenov — published its formal six-month progress report on the October 10, 2025 Gaza ceasefire. The report's central finding: 'At this stage, the principal obstacle to full implementation remains Hamas' refusal to accept verified decommissioning, relinquish coercive control, and permit a genuine civilian transition in Gaza.' The six-month report — covering October 10, 2025 through April 10, 2026 — documented that all four Board of Peace Phase Two deadlines (April 11, 14, 19, and a late-April window) had passed without Hamas agreement, and that Phase Two negotiations had not resumed in any substantive form. The report confirmed that Israel continued to control approximately 60% of Gaza's territory beyond the ceasefire's Yellow Line boundaries — characterizing this as a compliance issue on Israel's part — but placed ultimate blame for the Phase Two deadlock on Hamas's categorical refusal to accept the disarmament framework. The report noted that the Board of Peace's own May 6 announcement that it would NOT hold Israel to ceasefire compliance terms removed the principal diplomatic deterrent against Israeli war resumption. The Board's report also documented that less than $1 billion of $17 billion in pledged reconstruction funds had actually been received, with disbursement stalled pending Phase Two security guarantees. The UN-EU-World Bank joint assessment had estimated $71.4 billion total reconstruction cost. The Board of Peace simultaneously announced it would formally present the report to the UN Security Council in a scheduled Thursday, May 21, 2026 session — escalating the multilateral pressure on Hamas by bringing the Phase Two deadlock to the full Security Council. Hamas rejected the six-month report as containing 'fallacies that absolve the occupying government of its responsibilities,' reiterating its position that Hamas would not discuss disarmament without a guaranteed Israeli withdrawal and a political horizon toward Palestinian statehood.

media.caption: Hamas to blame for lack of progress on Phase Two of ceasefire, Board of Peace report says — Euronews, May 20, 2026
